title: Deterministic Verification and a Single-Repair Guardrail for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: a Paired, Shared‑Candidate Study
abstract: We report a sealed, preregistered paired experiment that measured the marginal verifier-detected effect of interposing a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair on the same LLM-generated configuration candidate. Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation call per intent reused for both episodes) we generated one candidate per natural-language intent with gpt-5-mini for N = 250 pairs and evaluated two episodes per intent: baseline (accept candidate) and guarded (deterministic_netops_validator_v5; if failing, permit a single automated repair). Execution completed 500 episodes with model_calls_used = 251. Results: baseline verifier-pass 249/250 (99.6%), guarded verifier-pass 250/250 (100.0%); contingency n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = +0.4 percentage points, 95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp] (paired bootstrap percentile, 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729), exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The preregistered sim‑to‑real (production-like) confirmatory contrast was not executed in this run; the reported confirmatory estimand applies only to the synthetic/emulation partition executed here. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived; a single representative manifest artifact (execution/raw_results.jsonl, SHA-256: 438fa6fa665160f917f0da85021f6e3102c9fcbc38a76fb5d6187f3a58d150d9) and the preregistration SHA-256 (7a984dbf7265c9a774eaf95c6c930dcf5f1e8845088bbc0e0855e3b4f1000ede) are cited in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are being explored as intent-to-configuration translators in network operations (NetOps). While LLMs can produce draft device CLI sequences, stochastic generation introduces operational risk: syntax errors, incorrect command ordering, local-policy violations, and vendor-CLI subtleties. Prior surveys and empirical work document both feasibility and remaining verification needs for LLM-generated configurations [1],[2].

A common architectural response is a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline that interposes a deterministic validator between generation and acceptance and, optionally, performs bounded automated repair when mechanically verifiable defects are detected [3],[4]. Such pipelines reduce mechanically checkable error classes (syntax, ordering, local-policy violations) but it remains empirically unclear how large the marginal verifier+single-repair effect is when modern LLM candidates are already highly conformant under constrained tasks.

This paper reports a preregistered paired experiment that isolates the marginal effect of a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair under explicit shared_initial_candidate semantics (the same initial generation is reused for both baseline and guarded episodes). Our primary contribution is an artifact-grounded quantification of that marginal effect for a constrained task bank (N_pairs = 250) and exact reconciliation of model calls and repair events.
sections.related_work:
Surveys and empirical studies establish that (a) LLMs can generate usable draft configurations in controlled setups [1],[2]; (b) deterministic verification tools (e.g., Batfish-style analyses, header-space/model checking) provide mechanized checks used as validators in GVR pipelines [4],[5]; and (c) generate-and-verify or verified-prompt workflows increase detection/correction rates for mechanically checkable defects in code/configuration domains, though deeper semantic correctness and cross-vendor subtleties remain challenging [6].

Security analyses of prompt-injection and retrieval-based threats emphasize the need for filtering and validation layers in LLM-integrated pipelines but note that adaptive adversaries remain an open threat [7]. Our work differs by using a preregistered paired design with shared_initial_candidate semantics that isolates the validator/repair marginal effect on identical model outputs and by archiving comprehensive validator traces and reconciliation artifacts for auditability.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The experiment was preregistered as study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 (preregistration SHA-256: 7a984dbf7265c9a774eaf95c6c930dcf5f1e8845088bbc0e0855e3b4f1000ede). The confirmatory design specified N_pairs = 250, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, and the primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The preregistration froze a single-repair policy, exclusion and contamination rules, and the analysis procedures (exact McNemar two-sided test and paired-bootstrap percentile CI, 10,000 resamples).

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and provider-call accounting (explicit). Per the preregistration and execution manifest, exactly one initial model-generation call was produced per intent and that identical generated candidate was reused for both baseline and guarded episodes (no independent first-pass generation per condition). Provider-call reconciliation shows model_calls_used = 251 which decomposes to 250 shared initial-generation calls plus 1 repair call; stage_counts observed are {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1}. The adapter audit records condition_counts with the adapter's internal labels (e.g., "shared" reflecting the shared initial-generation) while stage_counts provide the per-stage mapping used in reconciliation. These exact numeric reconciliation facts are preserved in the archived manifests and deterministic reconciliation artifact.

Task bank and validator. A deterministic task generator produced 250 constrained intent tasks encoding initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and difficulty labels (medium/hard/very_hard/extreme). Tasks exercised workflow constraints (e.g., make-before-break uplink switchover, paired-link atomic MTU changes) and protected interfaces that must not be modified; the full task manifest and representative payloads are archived.

Model and pipeline. The declared model for initial generation was gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json). For each intent we executed one shared initial generation. The guarded pipeline applied deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implementing full_intent_constraint_validation (CLI parsing, required_sequence ordering, workflow-constraint checks, and expected_final_state comparison). When validator.valid=false in a guarded episode, up to one deterministic template-driven repair attempt was permitted (syntactic reordering, splitting/joining commands, simple token-order fixes), followed by a re-submission to the validator; no multi-iteration repair or human escalation was allowed by design.

Inclusion, contamination, and analysis. Exclusion rules removed outputs that prevented deterministic verification (vendor-parser failures), or contained credential-like tokens or denylist matches. Contamination detectors would flag instruction-like embedded tokens; flagged items were to be excluded from the primary analysis. The preregistered primary analysis used paired_binary_analysis_v1 (exact McNemar two-sided test) and computed the paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). For transparency: the preregistered sim-to-real (production-like) confirmatory contrast described in the preregistration was not executed; the reported confirmatory inference applies only to the synthetic/emulation partition executed in this run.
sections.results:
Execution and reconciliation. Execution completed the preregistered confirmatory partition with planned_episode_count = 500 and completed_episode_count = 500; complete_pair_count = 250 and model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial-generation + 1 repair). No episodes were excluded for missingness or contamination in the confirmatory run.

Primary binary outcomes. Deterministic validator-scored successes: baseline_success_count = 249 (baseline_success_rate = 0.996), guarded_success_count = 250 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). Observed paired contingency: n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The single discordant pair (baseline failed, guarded passed) corresponds to the only exercised repair call; repair-conversion rate on the confirmatory partition = 1/250 = 0.004 (0.4%).

Statistical inference. Exact McNemar two-sided test on discordant counts (n10 = 1, n01 = 0) returned p = 1.0. The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval for the guarded − baseline paired difference (10,000 resamples; seed = 1729) is [0.0, 0.012] (i.e., 0 – 1.2 percentage points). Analysis artifacts (contingency table, condition summary, bootstrap parameters) are archived and referenced in the evidence bundle.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics and the constrained synthetic/emulation task bank, the marginal verifier-detected benefit of inserting deterministic validation plus a single automated repair was small: initial gpt-5-mini candidates satisfied the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases and the single permitted repair converted the sole failing candidate. The paired-bootstrap CI upper bound (1.2 percentage points) bounds the maximum verifier-detected improvement under these study conditions.

Why the small observed gain. Artifact-grounded reasons include: (1) the deterministic task generator encoded constrained intents and allowed_touched_fields that reduced ambiguity; (2) the declared model produced highly consistent, syntactically well-formed sequences for these constrained intents; and (3) the deterministic validator measured mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, ordering, expected_final_state) but not broader dynamic or emergent protocol correctness.

Power and scope. The preregistered power calculation assumed a baseline pass rate ≈ 0.90 and targeted detection of a 15 pp effect with N=250. The realized baseline pass rate (0.996) was substantially higher than assumed, which reduces power to detect small absolute improvements; consequently, the paired-bootstrap CI is the most informative practical bound here.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: results depend on prompt templates, the single-repair policy, and shared_initial_candidate semantics. Construct validity: the validator measures mechanically verifiable correctness but not live protocol dynamics. External validity: the confirmatory evidence covers only the synthetic/emulation partition; community and production-like partitions in the preregistration were not executed and remain exploratory. Security: adaptive prompt-injection and retrieval-based adversaries were not exercised.
sections.conclusion: We executed a sealed, preregistered paired experiment under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure the verifier-detected marginal effect of deterministic validation plus one permitted automated repair on identical LLM-generated configuration candidates. In N = 250 constrained synthetic intent tasks, initial gpt-5-mini candidates passed the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases; the guarded pipeline converted the single failing candidate via the one permitted repair. Observed paired improvement = 0.4 percentage points (95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp]; p = 1.0). We explicitly disclose that the preregistered sim‑to‑real confirmatory contrast was not executed and that the executed confirmatory estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline on the synthetic/emulation partition only. Broader production, adversarial, multi-model, and multi-iteration repair evaluations remain necessary to establish generality. Execution and analysis artifacts supporting these numeric claims are archived as described in the Disclosure Statement.

disclosure_statement:
Human role and autonomy boundary: After an autonomy lock required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track, the autonomous system performed literature search, study selection, preregistration freeze, prompt preservation, model calls, deterministic validation, permitted repair execution, analysis, drafting, peer-review, revision, and finalization without manual human editing of technical content. A human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and conducted pre-lock infrastructure development only.

Models, tools, and manifest pointer: Declared model used for initial generation = gpt-5-mini (provider recorded as openai_responses). Deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Deterministic task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. A representative archived manifest artifact for the run (execution/raw_results.jsonl) is recorded with SHA-256 = 438fa6fa665160f917f0da85021f6e3102c9fcbc38a76fb5d6187f3a58d150d9; the full execution and analysis bundle (task manifest, provider traces, validator traces, repair traces, reconciliation artifacts, and analysis CSVs) is archived as the evidence bundle referenced by that manifest entry.

Preregistration and master prompt (immutable references): Preregistration study id = study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1 (preregistration SHA-256 = 7a984dbf7265c9a774eaf95c6c930dcf5f1e8845088bbc0e0855e3b4f1000ede). Immutable master prompt initiating the autonomous run archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba.

Execution contract and deviation disclosure: The preregistration specified multiple partitions (synthetic/emulation, community, production-like) and a sim-to-real confirmatory contrast. Deviation disclosure: the preregistered sim-to-real (production-like) confirmatory comparison was not executed in this run; the executed confirmatory estimand reported here is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline evaluated on the synthetic/emulation partition only (N_pairs = 250) under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Provider-call reconciliation for the executed run is model_calls_used = 251 composed of 250 shared initial-generation calls plus 1 repair call, with observed stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 250, "repair": 1} (these exact reconciliation facts are archived in the evidence bundle).
limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed and remain exploratory.

Deterministic validator assessed mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, ordering, required-sequence, expected_final_state) but did not measure broader semantic or behavioral correctness (live protocol dynamics, emergent interactions).
Single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and one validator implementation were used; results do not establish multi-model or alternate-validator generality.
Only one automated repair attempt was permitted by design; multi-iteration repairs or human-in-the-loop escalation were not evaluated.
Adversarial and retrieval-based attacks (adaptive prompt-injection, vendor-targeted exploit vectors) and large-scale production heterogeneity were not exercised and remain open threats.
